posts.title: Warm Spinach & Walnut Salad
posts.meta_description: Warm spinach and walnut salad pairs briefly blanched greens with puréed walnuts and tamari for a simple, savory dish with soft texture and depth.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.93
posts.body_markdown:
Warm Spinach & Walnut Salad is built around speed: the spinach is blanched only until it wilts and turns bright green, then drained before it can overcook.

The walnuts are puréed instead of chopped, which lets them cling to the spinach and give the salad a fuller, almost creamy texture without adding a separate dressing.

Keep the final seasoning simple and measured. Bragg seasoning, tamari, or soy sauce supplies the salt and savoriness, so the finished dish needs very little else.

## Ingredients
- 5–6 cups spinach, chopped
- 1/2 cup walnuts
- 2 tablespoons Bragg all-purpose seasoning, tamari, or soy sauce

## Method
Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the spinach for only a few seconds, until just wilted and bright green. Drain and gently squeeze out excess water. Purée the walnuts in a blender or food processor. Combine the spinach, walnut purée, and seasoning in a large bowl, toss gently, and serve warm. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Thai Godot Salad
posts.meta_description: Thai Godot Salad layers baby spinach, peppers, sprouts, snap peas, herbs and crunchy nuts, finished with a bright Thai-style dressing.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.93
posts.body_markdown:
Thai Godot Salad is a large, highly textured bowl built from tender spinach, crisp peppers, sprouts, snap peas, cabbage, herbs, and crushed nuts.

The recipe works because no single vegetable dominates. Cilantro and Thai basil add a strong fresh note, while pecans or cashews bring enough richness to balance the raw vegetables.

The source pairs the salad with its Thai Salad Dressing rather than seasoning the vegetables separately. Toss only when ready to serve so the leaves and snap peas stay lively.

## Ingredients
- 6 cups baby spinach leaves
- 1 cup red bell peppers, chopped
- 1 cup yellow bell peppers, chopped
- 1/2 cup red onions, sliced
- 1 cup bean sprouts
- 1 cup sugar snap peas, ends trimmed and strings removed
- 1/2 cup pecans or cashews, crushed
- 3/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 3/4 cup Thai basil, chopped
- 1 cup Chinese curly cabbage, shredded
- Thai Salad Dressing

## Method
Place all of the vegetables, herbs, sprouts, snap peas, and crushed nuts in a large bowl. Toss together gently, add Thai Salad Dressing, and toss again until evenly coated. Serve immediately. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Cooling Couscous Salad
posts.meta_description: Cooling Couscous Salad combines fluffy couscous with tomato, cucumber, herbs, sun-dried tomato, feta and lemon for a chilled grain salad.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.94
posts.body_markdown:
Cooling Couscous Salad begins with couscous hydrated off the heat, which keeps the grains light and avoids unnecessary cooking once the water has boiled.

Tomato, cucumber, mint, parsley, green onion, sun-dried tomato, and feta bring several kinds of freshness and saltiness to the same bowl without making the dressing heavy.

Lemon or lime and a small amount of olive oil finish the salad. Chill it before serving so the couscous has time to absorb the vegetable and herb flavors.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- 5 cups water
- 3 1/2 cups couscous, uncooked
- 1 cup tomatoes, diced
- 1 cup cucumbers, diced
- 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup green onions, chopped
- 1/3 cup sun-dried tomatoes, chopped
- 1/2 cup feta cheese, crumbled
- Juice of 1 lemon or lime
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Bring the water and bouillon powder to a boil, stirring until dissolved. Remove from the heat, stir in the couscous, cover, and let stand for 5 minutes. Combine the remaining ingredients in a large bowl, add the couscous, mix well, and adjust the seasoning. Chill before serving. Makes 6 servings.

posts.title: Tabbouleh Twist with Olives & Walnuts
posts.seo_title: Tabbouleh Twist with Olives & Walnuts | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A tabbouleh variation with bulgur, parsley, mint, tomatoes, black olives and toasted walnuts, dressed simply with olive oil, lemon and garlic.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.95
posts.body_markdown:
This tabbouleh variation keeps the familiar parsley, mint, tomato, lemon, and cracked wheat base, then adds black olives and toasted walnuts for extra savoriness and texture.

The cracked wheat is soaked rather than simmered. Boiling water softens it in about ten minutes, leaving the cook free to prepare the herbs, vegetables, olives, and nuts separately.

Letting the finished salad sit briefly deepens the flavor because the wheat continues to absorb lemon, olive oil, and the juices released by the vegetables.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 cups cracked wheat or bulgur wheat
- 3 cups boiling water
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/3 cup green onions, chopped
- 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, chopped
- 1 cup tomatoes, diced
- 1/2 cup black olives, sliced
- 1/3 cup walnuts, toasted
- 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
- 4 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 clove garlic, minced

## Method
Combine the cracked wheat and boiling water in a large bowl and set aside. Mix the remaining ingredients in a second bowl. When the cracked wheat has absorbed the water, about 10 minutes, add it to the other ingredients and toss well. Let the salad stand for a short while before serving if you want a stronger, more settled flavor. Makes 6 servings.

posts.title: Millet with Sautéed Vegetables
posts.meta_description: Millet with sautéed zucchini, tomato and mushrooms is finished with tamari, rice vinegar and basil for a grain dish served warm or cold.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.96
posts.body_markdown:
Millet with Sautéed Vegetables is part grain salad and part warm vegetable dish. The millet cooks separately while the vegetables build flavor in the pan.

Onion is browned first, then zucchini, tomato, and mushrooms are cooked more gently so they soften without losing all of their structure. Tamari, vinegar, and basil are added near the end.

The final step is simply to fold the vegetables through the cooked millet. The source serves the dish either warm or cold, which makes it useful beyond one specific meal.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup millet
- 2 cups water
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 1 cup zucchini, finely sliced and quartered
- 1 1/2 cups tomatoes, diced
- 3/4 cup mushrooms, chopped
- 1 tablespoon tamari or soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon rice vinegar or lemon juice
- 1 teaspoon dried basil or 2 tablespoons fresh basil, chopped

## Method
Bring the millet and water to a boil, immediately reduce to a simmer, and cook until done, about 15 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and sauté the onions until they begin to brown. Add the zucchini, tomatoes, and mushrooms, reduce the heat to low, and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally; cover if the pan becomes dry. Add tamari, rice vinegar, and basil, cook for 5 minutes more, then fold the vegetables through the millet. Season to taste and serve warm or cold. Makes 6 servings.

posts.title: Geeta’s Buckwheat Noodle, Mango & Bell Pepper Salad
posts.seo_title: Geeta’s Buckwheat Noodle, Mango & Bell Pepper Salad | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Buckwheat noodles meet mango, red pepper, ginger, tamari and rice vinegar in a chilled salad finished with lime, cilantro and black sesame.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.97
posts.body_markdown:
Geeta’s Buckwheat Noodle, Mango & Bell Pepper Salad combines sweet mango with red pepper and a savory dressing based on tamari, vinegar, olive oil, and sesame oil.

The vegetables and fruit are dressed before the noodles are added. That gives the mango, onion, ginger, and pepper time to take on the salty and acidic seasoning while the noodles cook and cool.

The final lime, cilantro, and black sesame are added just before serving. That keeps the finish fresh even after the salad has spent a few hours in the refrigerator.

## Ingredients
- 1 red bell pepper, diced
- 1 mango, peeled and diced
- 3 tablespoons red onions, diced
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
- Dash of sesame oil
- 2 tablespoons tamari or soy sauce
- 2–3 tablespoons rice vinegar
- 2 bunches buckwheat noodles
- Juice of 1/2 lime
- 3 tablespoons fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- Black sesame seeds, for garnish

## Method
Combine the bell pepper, mango, red onion, ginger, olive oil, sesame oil, tamari, and rice vinegar in a large bowl and toss well. Cook the buckwheat noodles according to the package directions, drain, and cool. Add the cooled noodles to the bowl, toss, and refrigerate for a few hours. Just before serving, add the lime juice, cilantro, and black sesame seeds and toss again. Makes 6 servings.

posts.title: Rainbow Wild Rice Salad
posts.meta_description: Rainbow Wild Rice Salad mixes cooked wild rice with peppers, pecans, dried fruit, pineapple and water chestnuts in a rice-vinegar dressing.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.98
posts.body_markdown:
Rainbow Wild Rice Salad uses cooked wild rice as a sturdy base for peppers, nuts, dried fruit, pineapple, water chestnuts, and green onion.

The mix moves between crisp, chewy, sweet, and nutty textures, while the optional green chili provides a small amount of heat without changing the salad’s basic character.

The dressing is deliberately minimal: equal parts rice vinegar and olive oil. That keeps the grain and vegetables distinct instead of covering them with a heavier sauce.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups wild rice, cooked
- 1/2 cup red bell peppers, diced
- 1/2 cup yellow bell peppers, diced
- 1/4 cup pecans
- 2 tablespoons currants or cranberries
- 1/4 cup pineapple, chopped
- 1/2 cup water chestnuts, sliced
- 2 tablespoons green onions, white parts only, chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced, optional
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- 1/4 cup olive oil

## Method
Combine the cooked wild rice, bell peppers, pecans, dried fruit, pineapple, water chestnuts, green onions, and optional green chili in a medium bowl. Shake the rice vinegar and olive oil together in a jar, pour over the salad, toss well, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Light Lentil Salad
posts.meta_description: Green or brown lentils simmer with celery and carrot, then cool with lemon, parsley and salt for a light, portable salad with simple seasoning.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.99
posts.body_markdown:
Light Lentil Salad cooks the lentils, celery, and carrot together in vegetable stock, so the vegetables become part of the cooking liquid rather than a raw garnish.

Lemon juice is added after the pot comes off the heat. The acidity brightens the cooked lentils without interfering with the simmering stage, while parsley is saved until the mixture has cooled.

Watch the liquid as the lentils cook. The source notes that extra water can be added if the pot begins to dry before the lentils are soft.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup green or brown lentils
- 1 cup celery, diced
- 1/2 cup carrots, diced
- 1 1/2 cups vegetable stock
- 1/4 cup lemon juice
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped

## Method
Combine the lentils, celery, carrots, and vegetable stock in a large pot. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook until the lentils are soft, about 20 minutes, adding water if the liquid dries out too quickly. Remove from the heat, transfer to a bowl, and stir in the lemon juice. Let cool, then add the salt and parsley, toss, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Mixed Bean Salad
posts.meta_description: Chickpeas, black beans and kidney beans are tossed with lemon or vinegar, cumin, herbs, chili and olive oil, then chilled before serving.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.100
posts.body_markdown:
Mixed Bean Salad brings three cooked beans into one bowl: chickpeas, black beans, and red kidney beans. The combination gives the salad weight without requiring a cooked grain.

Garlic, green onion, cilantro, green chili, and cumin supply the aromatic side, while lemon juice or vinegar provides the acidity that keeps the beans from tasting flat.

The source gives the salad at least two hours in the refrigerator before serving. That rest is useful because the beans need time to absorb the seasoning fully.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 cups chickpeas, cooked or canned
- 1 1/2 cups black beans, cooked or canned
- 1 1/2 cups red kidney beans, cooked or canned
- 1–2 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 1–2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 tablespoons green onions, chopped
- 3 tablespoons fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 2 teaspoons fresh green chilies, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- 4 tablespoons lemon juice or vinegar

## Method
Combine all of the ingredients in a large bowl and mix thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours so the beans can absorb the seasoning. Taste again before serving and adjust the salt, pepper, or acidity if needed. Makes 6 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Sprouted Mixed Bean Salad
posts.meta_description: Cooked sprouted beans, red pepper, celery and onion are dressed with rice vinegar, olive oil, Dijon, garlic and herbs, then chilled.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.101
posts.body_markdown:
Sprouted Mixed Bean Salad starts with beans that have already been sprouted and cooked, then adds crisp red pepper, celery, and red onion.

The dressing is more structured than a plain vinaigrette: rice vinegar and olive oil are joined by Dijon, garlic, dried Italian herbs, maple syrup, salt, and pepper.

A short refrigeration period is part of the method, not an afterthought. The source rests the salad for at least half an hour so the beans can absorb the dressing.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups mixed beans, sprouted and cooked
- 1 cup red bell peppers, chopped
- 1 cup celery, chopped
- 1/4–1/2 cup red onions, minced
- 1/3 cup rice vinegar
- 1/3 cup olive oil
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon dried Italian herbs
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Combine the cooked sprouted beans, bell pepper, celery, and red onion in a medium bowl and toss. Shake the rice vinegar, olive oil, Dijon, garlic, herbs, maple syrup, salt, and pepper together in a jar. Pour the dressing over the salad, toss again, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving. Makes 4–5 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Picnic Medley Salad
posts.meta_description: Black beans, sweet corn, red pepper and parsley make a simple picnic salad finished with cider vinegar or lemon, olive oil and green chili.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.102
posts.body_markdown:
Picnic Medley Salad combines black beans and sweet corn with red bell pepper and a generous amount of parsley or cilantro. It is compact, colorful, and easy to transport.

The dressing is built from apple cider vinegar, another vinegar, or lemon juice, with olive oil and optional green chili. That gives the salad enough acidity without obscuring the vegetables.

Because the beans and corn are already cooked, the recipe is mostly assembly. The important part is tossing evenly so every portion gets both the dressing and the fresh herbs.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 cups black beans, cooked or canned
- 1 1/2 cups sweet corn kernels, cooked or canned
- 1 cup red bell peppers, diced
- 1 cup fresh parsley, chopped, or fresh cilantro leaves
- 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, another vinegar, or lemon juice
- 1/4 cup olive oil
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh green chilies, finely chopped
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Combine the black beans, corn, bell pepper, and parsley or cilantro in a large bowl and toss. Shake the vinegar or lemon juice, olive oil, green chili, salt, and pepper together in a jar. Pour over the salad, toss again until evenly coated, and serve. Makes 4 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: New Potato Salad
posts.meta_description: New potatoes are tossed warm with mayonnaise and olive oil, then combined with celery, shallot, parsley and optional egg for a simple potato salad.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.103
posts.body_markdown:
New Potato Salad keeps the potato skins on and dresses the potatoes while they are still warm. That helps the mayonnaise and olive oil coat the cut surfaces evenly.

Celery, shallot, parsley, and optional hard-boiled egg are mixed separately while the potatoes cook. Chili flakes are optional and should stay in the background.

The source serves the finished salad either slightly warm or chilled. Both work because the dressing is added before the potatoes have fully cooled.

## Ingredients
- 10–12 new potatoes, skins on
- 2 celery stalks, thinly sliced
- 1 shallot, minced
- 1 hard-boiled egg, diced, optional
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- Dash of chili flakes, optional
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 2 tablespoons mayonnaise
- 1 teaspoon olive oil

## Method
Place the potatoes in a large pot of salted water, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook until tender, about 15–20 minutes. While they cook, combine the celery, shallot, optional egg, salt, pepper, chili flakes, and parsley in a large bowl. Drain the potatoes and cut them into halves or quarters. Toss the warm potatoes with olive oil and mayonnaise, then fold them into the celery mixture. Serve slightly warm or chilled. Makes 2–4 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Calming Wakame Seaweed Salad
posts.meta_description: Wakame and salted cucumber are dressed with rice vinegar, sweetener and tamari for a simple seaweed salad with clean, subtle savory flavor.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.104
posts.body_markdown:
Calming Wakame Seaweed Salad depends on two separate preparation steps: the dried seaweed is soaked until tender, while the cucumber is salted and drained.

Those steps control the texture before the dressing is introduced. Softened wakame remains distinct from the crisp cucumber instead of turning the whole bowl watery.

Rice vinegar, sweetener, and tamari form the dressing. Let the finished salad sit briefly so the seaweed and cucumber can take on the seasoning before serving.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 pound wakame seaweed
- Room-temperature water, enough to cover the seaweed
- 1 1/2 cups cucumbers, thinly sliced
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- 1 tablespoon sweetener
- 3 tablespoons tamari or soy sauce

## Method
Cover the wakame with room-temperature water and soak until soft, about 15 minutes or longer if you prefer a softer texture. Place the cucumbers in a colander, sprinkle with salt, and drain for 30 minutes. Shake the rice vinegar, sweetener, and tamari together until the sweetener dissolves. Cut the softened wakame into bite-size pieces, gently squeeze excess water from the cucumbers, combine both in a serving bowl, add the dressing, and toss. Let stand for 5–10 minutes before serving. Makes 4–6 servings.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Everyday Salad Dressing
posts.meta_description: An everyday vinaigrette of olive oil, lemon or rice vinegar, garlic, maple syrup and Dijon, rested briefly so the sharp flavors settle.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.105
posts.body_markdown:
Everyday Salad Dressing is a balanced, flexible vinaigrette made from equal parts olive oil and lemon juice or rice vinegar, with garlic, maple syrup, and Dijon.

The garlic and mustard give the dressing definition, while the small amount of maple syrup rounds the acidity without turning the mixture noticeably sweet.

The source rests the dressing for at least thirty minutes before use. If it has been refrigerated, bringing it back toward room temperature loosens the olive oil again.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
- 1/4 cup lemon juice or rice vinegar
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup, or to taste
- 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Combine all ingredients in a jar and shake thoroughly until blended. Let the dressing stand for 30 minutes or longer before using so the flavors settle. If refrigerated, allow it to sit at room temperature before serving so the oil becomes fluid again. Makes about 1/2 cup.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Spicy French Dressing
posts.meta_description: A tangy French-style dressing with olive oil, cider vinegar, cayenne, mustard and Worcestershire, with optional honey or agave for balance.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.105
posts.body_markdown:
Spicy French Dressing is a sharp, full-flavored vinaigrette built from equal parts oil and vinegar, then seasoned with cayenne, mustard, and Worcestershire sauce.

The optional honey or agave softens the acidity and heat. It should dissolve completely, just as the mustard should be mixed in without leaving small clumps.

This dressing is assertive enough for simple green salads, sliced tomatoes, or vegetables with onion and herbs. A little goes a long way once the spices are evenly dispersed.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup olive oil, flaxseed oil, or hemp oil
- 1/2 cup apple cider vinegar, or another vinegar
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 1/2 teaspoon dry English mustard or Dijon mustard
- 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce
- 2 teaspoons honey or agave nectar, optional

## Method
Combine all ingredients in a jar and mix or shake thoroughly. Continue until the optional honey or agave has dissolved and the mustard is fully dispersed without clumps. Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving. Makes about 1 cup.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Fortifying Lemon & Garlic Dressing
posts.meta_description: Lemon and garlic lead this light dressing, with flaxseed or hemp oil and optional herbs; a short rest intensifies the savory, citrus flavor.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.106
posts.body_markdown:
Fortifying Lemon & Garlic Dressing is led by lemon and fresh garlic rather than a large volume of oil. The result is bright, direct, and strongly savory.

Flaxseed or hemp oil gives the dressing enough body to coat vegetables, while optional fresh or dried herbs can add another aromatic layer without changing the basic formula.

For a stronger garlic flavor, the source recommends a short rest in the refrigerator. Ten minutes is enough to let the garlic move more fully into the dressing.

## Ingredients
- 4–6 tablespoons lemon juice
- 4 tablespoons flaxseed oil or hemp oil
- 1–2 teaspoons garlic, minced
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1 tablespoon fresh herbs or 1/2 teaspoon dried herbs, optional

## Method
Combine all ingredients in a jar and shake well until blended. Use immediately for a lighter garlic flavor, or refrigerate for at least 10 minutes before serving if you want the garlic to become more pronounced. Makes about 1/2 cup.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Tridoshic Salad Dressing
posts.meta_description: A restrained salad dressing made from light olive oil, rice vinegar, salt and pepper, suited to raw vegetables and bitter greens.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.106
posts.body_markdown:
Tridoshic Salad Dressing is intentionally spare: light olive oil, rice vinegar, salt, and pepper. There is no sweetener, mustard, garlic, or heavy seasoning.

That restraint makes the dressing useful with vegetables whose own flavor should remain obvious, particularly daikon, carrot, endive, or watercress.

The technique is equally simple. Because there are so few ingredients, shake thoroughly and taste the balance of vinegar, oil, salt, and pepper before serving.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon light olive oil
- 1/4 cup rice vinegar
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Place the olive oil, rice vinegar, salt, and pepper in a jar. Shake until evenly combined, taste, and adjust the seasoning if needed. Use with raw vegetables or bitter greens. Makes about 1/4 cup.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Cleansing Lemon & Cumin Dressing
posts.meta_description: A simple lemon and cumin dressing combines fresh citrus, light olive oil and salt for a bright vinaigrette with warm spice in the background.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.107
posts.body_markdown:
Cleansing Lemon & Cumin Dressing pairs fresh lemon juice with a modest amount of ground cumin. The spice stays in the background rather than turning the dressing heavy.

Light olive oil softens the lemon while still keeping the vinaigrette sharp enough for raw vegetables and green salads. Salt is the only additional seasoning.

The title reflects the source, but the practical culinary idea is straightforward: lemon supplies the acidity, cumin adds warmth, and a quick shake brings them together.

## Ingredients
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 4 tablespoons light olive oil
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1/4 teaspoon salt, or to taste

## Method
Combine the lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, and salt in a jar. Shake well until the cumin is dispersed and the dressing is evenly blended. Taste for salt and use immediately. Makes about 1/2 cup.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Simple Olive Oil & Balsamic Vinegar Dressing
posts.seo_title: Simple Olive Oil & Balsamic Vinegar Dressing | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Extra-virgin olive oil and balsamic vinegar form a classic three-ingredient dressing with salt and pepper, mixed simply and ready in moments.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.107
posts.body_markdown:
Simple Olive Oil & Balsamic Vinegar Dressing is exactly what the title promises: olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper with nothing added to distract from them.

Because the formula is so short, the quality of the oil and vinegar matters more than it would in a dressing loaded with mustard, herbs, or sweetener.

The ratio favors olive oil but leaves enough balsamic to remain clearly acidic. Shake the mixture well just before use because it will naturally separate as it stands.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup olive oil
- 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Combine the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper in a jar. Shake vigorously until temporarily emulsified, then taste and adjust the seasoning. Shake again just before serving if the dressing has separated. Makes about 1 cup.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Thai Salad Dressing
posts.meta_description: Ginger, lime, tamari, olive and sesame oils, and maple syrup make a bright Thai-style dressing finished with chili, cilantro and basil.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.108
posts.body_markdown:
Thai Salad Dressing balances ginger, garlic, lime, tamari, olive oil, sesame oil, and maple syrup in a dressing that is salty, sour, aromatic, and lightly sweet.

The fresh green chili, cilantro, and basil are treated as salad garnishes rather than blended directly into the dressing. That keeps their texture and aroma distinct.

Shake the liquid dressing thoroughly first, then add the garnishes to the salad before pouring the dressing over. This preserves the separation between sauce and fresh herbs.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated or finely chopped
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 4 tablespoons lime juice
- 4 tablespoons olive oil
- Dash of sesame oil
- 1 tablespoon tamari, Bragg all-purpose seasoning, or soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon maple syrup
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced, or to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves, chopped

## Method
Combine the ginger, garlic, lime juice, olive oil, sesame oil, tamari or Bragg seasoning, and maple syrup in a jar and shake well. Add the green chili, cilantro, and basil directly to the salad. Toss, pour over the dressing, toss again, and serve. Makes about 1/2 cup dressing.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Creamy Cilantro Dressing
posts.meta_description: A yogurt-based cilantro dressing combines turmeric, lemon, coriander, cardamom, ginger, garlic and chili in a creamy, herb-forward sauce.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.109
posts.body_markdown:
Creamy Cilantro Dressing uses plain yogurt as the base, giving the dressing body without needing a large quantity of oil. Lemon keeps the texture from feeling too heavy.

Turmeric, coriander, cardamom, ginger, garlic, and green chili create a layered spice profile, while chopped cilantro gives the final dressing its fresh herbal character.

This is a mixing recipe rather than a cooking recipe. The main task is to distribute the ground spices, minced aromatics, and cilantro evenly through the yogurt.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup plain yogurt
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 2 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1/4 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/8 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 1/2 teaspoon maple syrup
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 clove garlic, crushed or minced
- Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, finely chopped

## Method
Place all ingredients in a bowl and mix thoroughly until the spices, aromatics, and cilantro are evenly distributed through the yogurt. Taste for salt and pepper, then use on salads or sliced vegetables. Makes about 1/2 cup.
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL

posts.title: Miso Dressing
posts.meta_description: Miso paste, honey, rice vinegar, hot water, tamari and sesame oil combine into a smooth, savory dressing for greens or steamed vegetables.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.109
posts.body_markdown:
Miso Dressing begins with a thick miso paste, so hot water is essential for loosening the mixture enough to become a pourable dressing.

Honey and rice vinegar create the sweet-sour balance, while tamari or Bragg seasoning reinforces the savory side. Only a small amount of sesame oil is needed for aroma.

Stir rather than shake this dressing until the miso is fully smooth. The finished sauce works well over wilted spinach or steamed vegetables, as suggested by the source.

## Ingredients
- 3/4 cup miso paste
- 3 tablespoons honey
- 3 tablespoons rice vinegar
- 2 tablespoons hot water
- 2 tablespoons Bragg all-purpose seasoning, tamari, or soy sauce
- 1/4 teaspoon sesame oil

## Method
Combine the miso paste, honey, rice vinegar, hot water, Bragg seasoning or tamari, and sesame oil in a bowl. Stir continuously until the miso is fully dissolved and the dressing is smooth and uniform. Makes about 1 cup.

posts.title: Clear Vegetable Soup
posts.meta_description: A clear vegetable soup and stock simmered with onion, carrot, celery, apple, herbs and whole spices, then strained for a fragrant, versatile broth.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.112
posts.body_markdown:
Clear Vegetable Soup is both a finished consommé and a base stock. Onion, carrot, celery, apple, herbs, and whole spices simmer together to build a fragrant broth.

The vegetables are chopped roughly because they will be strained out. Whole peppercorns, bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, turmeric, and optional ginger flavor the liquid during a long, gentle simmer.

The source also gives three variations: a more pungent version with garlic, lemon, and parsley; a French-style version with fennel and leeks; and a simpler version with fewer spices.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup onions, roughly chopped
- 1 1/4 cups carrots, roughly chopped
- 1 1/4 cups celery, roughly chopped
- 1/3 cup fresh cilantro leaves or parsley, roughly chopped
- 1 1/4 cups apples, roughly chopped
- 3 slices fresh ginger, optional
- 2 bay leaves
- 10 whole peppercorns
- 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
- 2 cloves
- Salt to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/4 cup fresh herbs, roughly chopped, such as thyme, sage, or mint
- 10 cups water

## Method
Combine all ingredients in a large pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Immediately reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 45 minutes. Strain before serving or using as stock. For the source’s first variation, add 3 whole garlic cloves, the juice of 1/2 lemon, and 1 cup roughly chopped parsley. For a French-style variation, add 1 fennel bulb, replace the onions with 2 sliced leeks, and omit the cloves, turmeric, cinnamon, ginger, and cilantro. For the simplest version, omit the cinnamon, ginger, and cilantro. Makes 8–10 cups.

posts.title: Acorn Squash Soup
posts.meta_description: Roasted acorn squash is simmered with ginger, cumin, turmeric, cinnamon and vegetable bouillon, then puréed and finished with parsley and yogurt.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.113
posts.body_markdown:
Acorn Squash Soup starts by roasting the squash before it enters the pot. That separates the softening of the squash from the later spice and broth stages.

Ginger, turmeric, cumin, chili, and cinnamon are layered into the soup before the water and bouillon finish the cooking. A small amount of agave or maple syrup rounds the squash’s natural sweetness.

The cinnamon stick and green chili are removed before blending. Purée carefully while the soup is hot, then finish each serving with parsley and a spoonful of yogurt.

## Ingredients
- 1 acorn squash
- 1 teaspoon good oil
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, finely chopped
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 fresh green chili, halved, or cayenne pepper to taste
- 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1 teaspoon vegetable bouillon powder
- 4 cups water
- 1 teaspoon agave nectar or maple syrup
- 1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
- 1/4 cup plain light yogurt, for garnish

## Method
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Halve the acorn squash and bake for 30–40 minutes, then cool, peel, and dice it. Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat, add the ginger for 30 seconds, then add turmeric, cumin, and green chili and cook for another 30 seconds. Add the squash, cinnamon, salt, bouillon, and water. Cover and cook until the squash begins to soften, then stir in the agave or maple syrup and continue until fully soft. Remove the cinnamon stick and chili, purée carefully until smooth, and garnish with parsley and yogurt. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Carrot Ginger Soup
posts.meta_description: Carrot Ginger Soup caramelizes onion and ginger before simmering with carrots, cinnamon and peppercorns, then purées the mixture until smooth.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.114
posts.body_markdown:
Carrot Ginger Soup gets much of its sweetness from the first stage, where onion and ginger cook slowly enough for the onions to caramelize before the liquid is added.

Carrots then simmer with cinnamon and whole peppercorns. The whole spices flavor the broth without being left in the final soup, so they are removed before blending.

The source also gives a thinner variation using extra water and vegetable bouillon. The base version remains smooth and concentrated, finished simply with chopped parsley.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 cups onions, chopped
- 4 teaspoons fresh ginger, minced
- 7 cups carrots, chopped
- 5 cups water
- 2 teaspoons salt
- 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
- 10 whole peppercorns
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a medium pot over medium-low heat. Add the onions and ginger and sauté until the onions caramelize, about 5–8 minutes. Stir in the carrots, water, salt, cinnamon stick, and peppercorns. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to a simmer, and cook until the carrots are tender, about 15–20 minutes. Remove the cinnamon stick and peppercorns, then purée carefully until smooth. Garnish with parsley and serve. For the thinner variation from the source, add 1–2 cups additional water and 1–2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder. Makes 6–8 servings.
